Member-only story Self Improvement Productivity Life Lessons Product Management Focus Your Life Is a Backlog With No Product Manager Why capable, ambitious people end up busy for years and ship almost nothing, and the fix product teams use every week Mohit Aggarwal 7 min read · Oct 30, 2026 -- Listen Share Press enter or click to view image in full size You are not lazy. You’re busy most evenings. You have a notes app full of genuinely good ideas. An online course sitting at 40% complete. A side business you’ll “properly start in January”. A book half-read on the nightstand and another three in the basket. A career you describe as “keeping my options open”. And yet, if you’re honest, the last three years look a lot like the three before them. Meanwhile someone you went to school with, not obviously smarter, not obviously harder working, picked one boring thing in 2021 and just kept doing it. Now they’re the person people call. What’s going on? I’m a product manager. I don’t have a psychology degree and I’m not a life coach. But I’ve spent eight years watching products fail, and I’ve noticed something uncomfortable. The way most promising products die is exactly the way most promising people stall. Not from bad ideas. From too many good ones.
